title: Sinusoidal – Battle a Language Model and Hack Its Brain
tools: Godot 4 (GDScript, shaders) · Qwen3.5-2B · PyTorch steering vectors · Sparse autoencoders · PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
blurb: A 3D card roguelike in Godot against a small language model; cutting wires in its head adds steering vectors that change how it speaks and plays.
long: A 3D card roguelike with a dark, low-res look: a branching map of battles and events, with three candles as lives.

The opponent, the Dealer, is a real language model (Qwen3.5-2B). Its head opens to show four wires; cutting one adds a steering vector to its activations, and players learn what each wire does by watching the Dealer change.
Sandbox modes turn interpretability papers into game mechanics, such as a gauge that tracks persona traits in the Dealer's responses. It is a work in progress; the card portraits are placeholders.
highlights: Opponent is a real Qwen3.5-2B with four cuttable steering wires
Persona grafts move their own gauge 5–12 standard deviations (single run)
Concept injection: 0 of 120 pilot trials noticed on 2B
Headless tests drive 40 bot runs through the map
